operations.name: admin_console.admin_get_runtime_config
operations.summary: Hot-reloadable configuration overrides (「授权 / 并发」panel).

operations.name: admin_console.admin_prune_task_events
operations.summary:
Trim every terminal task's event history to the retention limit.

Manual counterpart of the daily ``prune_task_events_job`` sweep. ``keep_last``
defaults to the hot-reloadable ``task_event_retention`` runtime-config value;
a request may override it (clamped to the same 100..1_000_000 bounds).

operations.name: ai.update_draft
operations.summary: Inline edit: fix the last 5% of an output, then approve as a whole.

operations.name: ai.usage_stats
operations.summary: Token usage per project — aggregated from each draft's meta.usage.

operations.name: audit_trash.audit_log_actions
operations.summary: Distinct actions and actors, so the filter dropdowns reflect real data.

operations.name: audit_trash.audit_logs_csv
operations.summary:
Download the *filtered* audit log as CSV.

Deliberately server-side rather than exporting the rows the browser happens
to have loaded: the table pages 50 at a time, so a client-side export would
hand the reviewer a file that looks complete and covers the first page only.

operations.name: audit_trash.list_trash
operations.summary: Everything the project has deleted, with its remaining retention.

operations.name: audit_trash.purge_from_trash
operations.summary: Delete one entry for real, ahead of its retention date.

operations.name: auth.config
operations.summary:
Canonical editor/collab protocol config (single source of truth).

Serves the sheet catalogue (keys + labels), the default sheet, the per-sheet
steps field map and the CRDT/room naming prefixes so the frontend consumes
one schema instead of re-declaring it in ``editor.js`` / ``collab.js``.

operations.name: auth.download_cli
operations.summary:
Download the standalone CLI that matches this server's API.

A single-file Python 3.10+ zipapp using only the standard library; run it
with ``python silver-cli.pyz --help``. It holds no credentials or server
data, so it is public like ``/health``.

operations.name: auth.register
operations.summary:
Self-service registration for LAN users.

Disabled unless ``LM_ALLOW_REGISTRATION`` is on. On success, an ``active``
account is logged in immediately (session + CSRF token established, mirroring
login); a ``disabled`` account (approval mode) is created in a pending state
and the client is told to wait for an administrator.

operations.name: dashboard.list_project_categories
operations.summary:
Distinct テスト区分 in this project, with names and case counts.

Exists so the routing editor can offer the 区分 that actually exist instead
of making an admin type them from memory: a mistyped 区分 produces a rule
that never matches, and nothing in the UI would ever say so.

operations.name: dashboard.project_dashboard_data
operations.summary:
Progress, trend, per-version and review aggregates for one project.

Served as a single bundle rather than four endpoints so the page cannot
render a progress ring and a review funnel computed seconds apart.

Gated on ``project.view``: this is a read-only summary of data the member
can already see row by row, so requiring a stronger capability would only
push people back to counting cells by hand.

operations.name: dashboard.test_run_history
operations.summary: Return paged matrix-backed run summaries for one exact test id.

operations.name: dashboard.test_run_history_csv
operations.summary: Stream the complete project-scoped run history as a safe CSV.

operations.name: dashboard.version_compare
operations.summary:
Compare latest non-cancelled results for two model identities.

``project.view`` is enough, so a reader can open it. ``left`` and ``right``
are ``name@version``; a model with no version is the bare name. Detail rows
carry ``row_uuid`` for the matrix, not a task key.

operations.name: imports_exports.export_const
operations.summary: Export the project's Const rows as a flat-table .xlsx.

operations.name: imports_exports.export_io
operations.summary: Export the project's 入出力 pool rows as a flat-table .xlsx.

operations.name: imports_exports.export_libfunc
operations.summary: Export the project's Lib(Func) rows as a block-structured .xlsx.

operations.name: imports_exports.export_test_matrix
operations.summary:
Export the editor's items as a byte-compatible Japanese Test-Matrix
workbook (summary sheet + per-category detail sheets).

operations.name: imports_exports.extract_io
operations.summary:
Harvest I/O signal declarations from step procedures into the 入出力 pool.

Scans the ``input_signals`` / ``expected_signals`` of the requested sheets'
step docs (``lib`` by default; ``test`` optionally), de-duplicates on
name+path, and merges the result into the pool with the same uniqueness and
per-row error reporting as an Excel import.

operations.name: imports_exports.import_const
operations.summary:
Import a Const workbook: one constant definition -> one editor row
(const_* fields).

operations.name: imports_exports.import_io
operations.summary:
Import an 入出力 (I/O signal pool) workbook: one signal -> one editor row
(io_name / io_path / io_note), keeping name AND path unique.

operations.name: imports_exports.import_libfunc
operations.summary:
Import a Lib(Func) workbook: one function block -> one editor row
(lib_* fields + shared step-detail JSON).

operations.name: imports_exports.import_test_matrix
operations.summary: Create a validated preview job for the Japanese Test-Matrix workbook.

operations.name: items.add_pool_entry
operations.summary:
Add one reference-pool row (``io`` / ``const``) from the step editor.

REST path only: when collaboration is live the client inserts through the
shared Y.Doc instead (this endpoint is then collab-blocked). Provisions the
pool's field set on demand and enforces its uniqueness contract server-side.

operations.name: items.ensure_pool_fields
operations.summary:
Provision a reference pool's field set (``io`` / ``const``) so its columns
render. Idempotent; used by the collaboration path, where rows are inserted
through the Y.Doc but the field definitions still live in the DB.

operations.name: me.me_create_token
operations.summary:
Issue a personal API token. The secret appears only in this response.

Body: ``name`` (1-64 chars), ``expires_days`` (1-365) and optional
``replace`` (revoke your active tokens of the same name). Requires a
password session, so a leaked token cannot mint further tokens.

operations.name: me.me_list_tokens
operations.summary: The caller's personal API tokens (secrets are never returned again).

operations.name: me.me_notifications
operations.summary:
List notifications for one scope (``unread`` | ``history`` | ``all``).

The legacy ``?unread=1`` flag still works so an older cached page keeps
functioning after a deploy.

operations.name: me.me_notifications_archive
operations.summary:
File notifications away into history.

Archiving is not deleting: "I have dealt with this" and "this never
happened" are different statements, and only the first one is safe to make
on the user's behalf. Archived rows also stop being revived by the
collapsing window, which is what made dismissed items reappear.

operations.name: me.me_notifications_clear_history
operations.summary: Drop read/archived rows only. Unread rows are outstanding work and stay.

operations.name: me.me_notifications_unread_count
operations.summary: Cheap endpoint for the 30s badge poll -- one COUNT, no row payload.

operations.name: me.me_overview
operations.summary: KPI band + the user's projects with their task mix.

operations.name: me.me_tasks
operations.summary:
Tasks across every project the user can see.

Query params: ``status``, ``mine=1``, ``project_id``, ``q``, ``limit``.

operations.name: models.deprecate_project_model
operations.summary: Hide a superseded model from the pickers without deleting its history.

operations.name: models.update_project_model_version
operations.summary:
Relabel a registered model (version + release note).

Separate from model creation on purpose: a version label is usually decided
*after* the model has been uploaded and smoke-tested, and re-labelling
changes how future test evidence is grouped, so it is an audited operation
of its own rather than a silent field edit.

operations.name: projects.collab_token
operations.summary:
Mint a short-lived signed token for the real-time collaboration socket.

Requires ``item.edit`` (only editors join the CRDT room; readers keep using
the REST read path). The separate collab server verifies this token — signed
with the shared ``SECRET_KEY`` — on connect. See design doc §8.

operations.name: reviews.assign_item_reviewer
operations.summary: Assign or clear the reviewer of a row.

operations.name: reviews.decide_exemptions_bulk
operations.summary:
Approve/reject many 不要 claims at once, with one shared reason.

Bulk is allowed (unlike ``Untestable``) because 不要 is normally decided per
feature area, but the note is still required and is written onto every row,
so no approval is left without a justification.

operations.name: reviews.decide_item_exemption
operations.summary: Approve or reject one 不要 claim. A note is mandatory either way.

operations.name: reviews.list_project_exemptions
operations.summary:
Cases claiming 項目作成 = 不要, by decision state.

Listing also routes freshly-typed claims (:func:`sync_pending`). Pending is
derived, so this only stamps a reviewer and rings a bell -- a claim is in
the queue whether or not this endpoint is ever called.

operations.name: reviews.list_project_reviews
operations.summary: Pending reviews in one project, optionally only the caller's own queue.

operations.name: reviews.review_item
operations.summary: Approve or reject a single pending review.

operations.name: reviews.review_items_bulk
operations.summary:
Approve/reject many rows at once.

Only verdicts declared bulk-approvable are accepted; ``Untestable`` rows are
reported back in ``skipped`` so the reviewer sees exactly what still needs an
individual decision instead of silently believing the queue is empty.

operations.name: reviews.set_review_policy
operations.summary:
Set which verdicts require sign-off in this project.

Project-level because it is a team policy, not a product decision: a
safety-critical project reviews every PASS, an exploratory one reviews
nothing.

operations.name: tasks.delete_project_tasks_batch
operations.summary:
Delete several of a project's tasks (and their workspaces) at once.

Body: ``{"keys": ["T000001", ...]}``. Requires ``task.delete``; each key is
resolved within the project so cross-project deletion is impossible.

operations.name: tasks.download_project_tasks_batch
operations.summary:
Bundle the reports of several of a project's tasks into one zip.

Query: ``?keys=T000001,T000002`` (or repeated ``keys`` params). Requires
``task.download``; keys are resolved within the project.

operations.name: tasks.project_latest_tasks
operations.summary: The newest run of every test id, with no recent-window truncation.

operations.name: tasks.rerun_selected_tasks
operations.summary:
Re-queue existing tasks by ``task_key`` ("重新测试" / retest).

Each chosen task is re-run with the model it was originally submitted with:
the JSON-runner inputs are regenerated from the current project ``test`` /
``lib`` / ``const`` sheet rows and the task row is reset to QUEUED and
enqueued (the stored result is overwritten). Live attempts are skipped,
stale queued rows can be retried, and tasks whose ``test_id`` no
longer exists in the project sheets are reported as missing.

operations.name: tasks.run_selected_tasks
operations.summary:
Queue the chosen ``test`` rows for JSON-runner execution (no upload).

The three runner inputs (``testcase_<id>.json`` / ``lib.json`` /
``constants.json``) are generated straight from the project's ``test`` /
``lib`` / ``const`` sheet rows, then the task is upserted by ``test_id``
(a re-run overwrites the stored result) and enqueued.

operations.name: tasks.task_preflight
operations.summary:
Reference data the submit form needs to warn *before* an upload.

Only the module-name vocabulary lives here. The counts the preflight bar
also shows (models, licence) already ride along on ``list_project_tasks``,
so this endpoint deliberately adds no queries.

``stdlib`` is served rather than hard-coded in JavaScript on purpose:
the authoritative set is ``sys.stdlib_module_names``, a *runtime* value that
differs between Python versions. A copy pinned in the front end would drift
from the interpreter that actually runs the judges, and the failure mode of
a stale copy is the worst kind -- a confident warning about a module that is
perfectly fine, which teaches people to ignore the warnings.

operations.name: tasks.upload_project_tree
operations.summary:
Upload a test-case folder tree and queue the chosen test ids for a
project. Only project members reach this (``task.upload``).
